metaDescription: UPLB Seedless Red mabolo is a mabolo variety from Crop Science Cluster. UPLB. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: UPLB Seedless Red is a registered mabolo variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2012 as NSIC 2012 MI 01. Crop Science Cluster. UPLB bred it. Its record notes a yield of 40.

Key facts about UPLB Seedless Red mabolo

blocks.caption: Key facts of UPLB Seedless Red

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of UPLB Seedless Red was about 32 years old and about 5 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 40. It bears every year, with fruit in July September. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

A fruit of UPLB Seedless Red weighs about 378.75 grams, and its shape is obloid. The flesh is cream and smooth. Its sweetness measured 13.24 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 85.56 percent of the fruit. Its fruiting season is July September, bearing annual.
Where and when to plant UPLB Seedless Red mabolo

Pick a variety by the fruit your buyers pay for: its size, sweetness and flesh, and how regularly the tree bears. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.a: The record shows a recorded yield of 40. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of UPLB Seedless Red?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
